title: Five-part leukocyte entropy does not establish incremental airflow-obstruction prediction in a separate NHANES sample
abstract: Adding five-part leukocyte entropy to a flexible clinical/count baseline did not establish improved prebronchodilator obstruction prediction in 2,473 NHANES 2009–10 adults: weighted Brier gain -0.00012727 (conditional-source 95% target-PSU bootstrap interval -0.00063013 to 0.00049558). Frozen models fitted in 2,252 NHANES 2007–08 adults were evaluated without refitting in the separately sampled 2009–10 cycle. Stronger count-interaction baselines and smoking/illness subgroup checks did not establish improved prediction. This is a cross-sectional negative feature-engineering experiment, not COPD diagnosis, equivalence or evidence of clinical utility.
